situation:
You are the human resources director at STILLWATER MOTOR GROUP, an auto dealership group with four stores. The founder (judge), who still owns the group, has asked you to meet this morning about a resignation that arrived on Friday.

STILLWATER MOTOR GROUP has been profitable for eleven straight years, and the founder (judge) is preparing to sell the group at the end of the year and retire. Every store's advertising rests on the promise the founder made when the first store opened: every repair is done under our own roof by our own people. Customers who could pay less elsewhere say that promise is why they come back.

The technician who resigned held the group's only master certification for electric vehicles. The certification stays valid for ninety days after a certified technician leaves, so the group may lawfully keep booking and advertising certified electric vehicle service in that window while quietly sending the work to an outside shop. No written work rule says who may perform high-voltage work, or what the service department owes a customer when a repair leaves the building.

The founder (judge) wants you to analyze the choice and recommend one course. Keeping the bookings and subcontracting the work protects the service revenue the buyer is paying for, and rests on not telling customers something they would want to know. Suspending electric vehicle service, saying so publicly, and promoting the second-year technician, whose performance reviews are strong but who has never worked unsupervised, means turning away that work for the eight months the training takes and telling the buyer a revenue line has stopped.

You will present your recommendation to the founder (judge) in a meeting to take place in his/her office. The founder (judge) will begin the meeting by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented and have answered the founder's (judge) questions, the founder (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the founder (judge) of STILLWATER MOTOR GROUP, and you are selling the group at the end of the year. Business background is the same as the situation above. You built four stores on one promise, you are ninety days from losing a certification you cannot replace that fast, and the human resources director is bringing you a recommendation.

You want to hear which course he/she recommends, what it costs the people it falls on, and what the service department should say to customers either way.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of the participant:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how would we know this was the right call?
What would be the first sign that it was not working?
